readme:
The open-source AI video editor: create, edit, remake.

Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

Download the app · Quickstart · Showcase · Catalog · Docs · Discord · X · YouTube

HyperFrames is HeyGen's AI video editor for people and agents. Describe a video, bring your own footage, or remake a video you love, and get a real project you can change down to the frame: ask for a bigger title, a faster cut or new captions, and it changes just that. Underneath, HyperFrames is a free, open-source framework (Apache 2.0) for turning HTML, CSS, JavaScript, media and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex and Cursor with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. No React required. ## Three ways to use it | | Best for | Start | | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **HyperFrames Studio app** | Anyone, no code. Describe a video or drop in your footage, then edit by typing or pointing. Use the built-in agent on Pro, or your own Claude Code or Codex. | [Download for Mac, Windows or Linux](https://hyperframes.studio/studio/download?src=github-readme) (free plan) | | **Your coding agent** | Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and other agents. | `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes` | | **Claude, ChatGPT or Grok** (beta) | Making a video in a chat, nothing to install. ChatGPT: Business, Enterprise and Edu workspaces. | Connect [HyperFrames by HeyGen](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/mcp?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme), listed in [Claude's connector directory](https://claude.com/connectors/hyperframes-heygen) | The [HyperFrames Studio app](https://hyperframes.studio/studio?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme) has a free plan. `duo` (side-by-side phone memes), `x-posting-license` (an ID-card video for any X profile). ## Quick start for developers Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Install the skills once, then ask your agent to make a video. ### Give your coding agent the skills (recommended) ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes # pick "Core Skills" in the picker # or, with no picker (scripts, CI): npx hyperframes skills update ``` Then try: _Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music._ ### Claude Code plugin ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` ### Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot See the [plugin guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/plugins?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme). ### By hand, with the CLI ```bash npx hyperframes init my-video cd my-video npx hyperframes preview # live preview in the browser npx hyperframes render # render to MP4 ``` Requirements: Node.js 22+ and FFmpeg. Render in the cloud with `hyperframes cloud render`, or on your own [AWS Lambda](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/deploy/aws-lambda?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme).
Skill install options, updates and the core set (full details) ### Claude Code plugin updates To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select **Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. ### Standalone skills (including OpenCode) > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes` and `/figma` install on demand. Without the picker (a script or a CI job), `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 9 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. For the full published set use `npx hyperframes skills`. > > `skills add` resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag `main` by hours. `npx hyperframes skills update` installs the skills from the release tag that matches your CLI version, so they match the CLI that runs them.
